02 | South 01.title: Nursery on Schenkweg
02 | South 01.body: A study of the trees and roads at the edge of The Hague. This early drawing is not a work from his childhood.
02 | South 01.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 1972.118.281

02 | South 02.title: Gardener by an Apple Tree
02 | South 02.body: A print of an ordinary worker bending beside a fruit tree. The subject reflects his sustained interest in labour.
02 | South 02.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 2021.241

02 | South 03.title: Avenue of Pollard Birches and Poplars
02 | South 03.body: Repeated pen strokes pull the eye down a quiet avenue at Nuenen.
02 | South 03.credit: The Art Institute of Chicago · Public-domain image via Wikimedia Commons · 2022.74

02 | South 04.title: A Peasant Woman Digging in Front of Her Cottage
02 | South 04.body: The peasant woman, modest cottage, and soil join in an image of rural life rather than a pastoral idyll.
02 | South 04.credit: The Art Institute of Chicago · Public-domain image via Wikimedia Commons · 1968.92

02 | South 05.title: The Potato Peeler
02 | South 05.body: An everyday task illuminated in dark brown tones. Vincent painted a Paris self-portrait on the reverse of this canvas later.
02 | South 05.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 67.187.70b

02 | South 06.title: The Potato Eaters (lithograph)
02 | South 06.body: Vincent made this lithograph himself. It is distinct from the oil painting of the same subject.
02 | South 06.credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington · Open Access / CC0 · 1951.10.33

01 | Fan 01 | painting.title: Road in Etten
01 | Fan 01 | painting.body: Made after Vincent began to study drawing in earnest. His childhood and earlier occupations are told through archival material and film, not through later paintings.
01 | Fan 01 | painting.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 459193

03 | South 01.title: Montmartre Windmill
03 | South 01.body: Montmartre windmills became a testing ground for brighter colour and a lighter touch.
03 | South 01.credit: Image: Wikimedia Commons · Public domain; see source page for version and collection

03 | South 02.title: Self-Portrait with a Straw Hat
03 | South 02.body: One of many Paris self-portraits in which Vincent experimented with colour and expression.
03 | South 02.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 436532

03 | South 03.title: Sunflowers (Paris)
03 | South 03.body: Cut sunflower heads laid on a table, not the later Arles sunflowers arranged in a vase.
03 | South 03.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 436524

03 | South 04.title: Portrait of Julien Tanguy
03 | South 04.body: Japanese prints behind Père Tanguy show how Vincent absorbed new colour and compositional ideas in Paris.
03 | South 04.credit: Image: Wikimedia Commons · Public domain; see source page for version and collection

03 | South 05.title: Bridge in the Rain (after Hiroshige)
03 | South 05.body: A painted interpretation of a print by Hiroshige, rather than an original view of Japan.

03 | North 01.title: Flowering Plum Orchard (after Hiroshige)
03 | North 01.body: Seen alongside Bridge in the Rain, this work explores Japanese outlines, colour fields, and framing.

04 | Fan 01 | painting.title: The Flowering Orchard
04 | Fan 01 | painting.body: Spring blossoms and a clear sky mark Vincent’s arrival in the south of France.
04 | Fan 01 | painting.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 436527

04 | Fan 02 | painting.title: Oleanders
04 | Fan 02 | painting.body: Flowers and tabletop objects show the increasingly bold colours of the Arles period.
04 | Fan 02 | painting.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 436530

04 | Fan 03 | painting.title: The Yellow House
04 | Fan 03 | painting.body: The house embodied his hope of making a shared place for artists to live and work.

04 | Fan 04 | painting.title: Café Terrace at Night
04 | Fan 04 | painting.body: A street illuminated at night; it is a different painting from the indoor Night Café.

04 | Fan 05 | painting.title: The Night Café
04 | Fan 05 | painting.body: An interior night scene whose strong red and green contrasts create a charged atmosphere.

04 | South 01.title: Madame Roulin and Her Baby
04 | South 01.body: One of the portraits of the Roulin family, people Vincent knew during his time in Arles.
04 | South 01.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 459123

04 | South 02.title: Street in Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer
04 | South 02.body: A work on paper from his visit to the Mediterranean coast at Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer.
04 | South 02.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 336318

05 | South 01.title: Van Gogh's Chair
05 | South 01.body: A plain wooden chair with Vincent’s pipe and tobacco; a counterpart to Gauguin’s chair.

05 | South 02.title: Gauguin's Chair
05 | South 02.body: A darker armchair, books, and candlelight contrast with the chair Vincent painted for himself.

05 | South 03.title: The Lullaby (Augustine Roulin)
05 | South 03.body: A portrait of Madame Roulin made after Vincent’s crisis, distinct from the 1888 mother-and-baby portrait.
05 | South 03.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 437984

05 | South 04.title: The Woman from Arles (Madame Ginoux)
05 | South 04.body: A portrait of the café owner, in the version held by The Metropolitan Museum of Art.
05 | South 04.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 436529

05 | South 05.title: Self-Portrait with Bandaged Ear
05 | South 05.body: A self-portrait during recovery, with a Japanese print behind him; the pipe version is a separate work.
05 | South 05.credit: Image: Wikimedia Commons · Public domain; see source page for version details

06 | Curved wall -1 0.title: Wheat Field with Cypresses
06 | Curved wall -1 0.body: Wheat, clouds, and cypresses show the rhythmic brushwork of the Saint-Rémy period.
06 | Curved wall -1 0.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 436535

06 | Curved wall -1 1.title: Olive Trees
06 | Curved wall -1 1.body: Olive groves became a repeated subject for observing light and season.
06 | Curved wall -1 1.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 437998

06 | Curved wall -1 2.title: Irises (in a vase)
06 | Curved wall -1 2.body: An arrangement of irises in a vase, not the broad garden view displayed nearby.
06 | Curved wall -1 2.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 436528

06 | Curved wall -1 3.title: Cypresses
06 | Curved wall -1 3.body: A monumental cypress studied within the landscape of southern France.
06 | Curved wall -1 3.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 437980

06 | Curved wall -1 4.title: First Steps, after Millet
06 | Curved wall -1 4.body: An interpretation after Millet, translating a printed source into Vincent’s own painted language.
06 | Curved wall -1 4.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 436526

06 | Curved wall 1 0.title: Corridor in the Asylum
06 | Curved wall 1 0.body: An actual corridor at the asylum, set against landscapes shaped by observation and imagination.
06 | Curved wall 1 0.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 336327

06 | Curved wall 1 1.title: Women Picking Olives
06 | Curved wall 1 1.body: Labourers become part of the moving rhythm of the olive trees.
06 | Curved wall 1 1.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 436536

06 | Curved wall 1 2.title: The Starry Night
06 | Curved wall 1 2.body: An imagined night sky composed with memories of the view from Saint-Rémy.

07 | Horizon -1 0.title: Portrait of Doctor Gachet or Man with a Pipe
07 | Horizon -1 0.body: An etching of Doctor Gachet, distinct from the two celebrated oil portraits.
07 | Horizon -1 0.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art · Open Access / CC0 · 849056

07 | Horizon -1 1.title: The Church at Auvers
07 | Horizon -1 1.body: The village landmark is transformed by animated lines and colour.

07 | Horizon -1 2.title: Daubigny's Garden
07 | Horizon -1 2.body: One version of a garden Vincent painted several times at Auvers.

07 | Horizon -1 3.title: Wheatfield under Thunderclouds
07 | Horizon -1 3.body: A wide wheatfield under dark clouds, opening the landscape horizontally.

07 | Horizon -1 4.title: Wheatfield with Crows
07 | Horizon -1 4.body: Often mistaken for an established final painting; that identification is not certain.

07 | Horizon 1 0.title: Tree Roots
07 | Horizon 1 0.body: Possibly among Vincent’s last paintings. The intertwined roots resist a single, definitive interpretation.

02 | North 01.title: Sorrow
02 | North 01.body: A drawing of Sien, identified here as the F929 / JH129 version rather than every work of the same subject.
02 | North 01.credit: Image: Wikimedia Commons · Public domain; source file credits Christie's

02 | North 02.title: The Potato Eaters (oil painting)
02 | North 02.body: The lamplit peasant family brings together studies of faces, interiors, and rural labour from his Nuenen years.
02 | North 02.credit: Image: Wikimedia Commons · Public domain; original held by the Van Gogh Museum

04 | South 03.title: Sunflowers (Arles, London version)
04 | South 03.body: Sunflowers in a vase painted for the Yellow House; separate from the cut Paris sunflower studies.
04 | South 03.credit: Image: Wikimedia Commons · Public domain; The National Gallery, London, NG3863

04 | South 04.title: Starry Night over the Rhône
04 | South 04.body: The Rhône at night, with lamplight reflected in the water. Not the later Starry Night of Saint-Rémy.
04 | South 04.credit: Image: Wikimedia Commons · Public domain; original held by the Musée d'Orsay

05 | South 06.title: The Red Vineyard
05 | South 06.body: Autumn grape harvest in interwoven reds and yellows, painted during Gauguin’s stay in Arles.
05 | South 06.credit: Image: Wikimedia Commons · Public domain; source file names the Pushkin Museum

06 | Curved wall 1 3.title: Almond Blossom
06 | Curved wall 1 3.body: Flowering branches painted for Vincent’s newborn nephew, also named Vincent.
06 | Curved wall 1 3.credit: Image: Wikimedia Commons · Public domain; original held by the Van Gogh Museum

06 | Curved wall 1 4.title: Irises (garden)
06 | Curved wall 1 4.body: Irises growing in the asylum garden; a different work from the vase of flowers.
06 | Curved wall 1 4.credit: Image: Getty Open Content, via Wikimedia Commons · Public domain; Getty collection 826
